ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory electronic screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and signatories against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit watch-list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) black and grey lists, and the United Kingdom Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list. Enhanced due diligence is triggered upon any positive or partial match, any connection to a FATF grey-listed jurisdiction, or any transaction involving a Politically Exposed Person within the last twelve months. Records of screening results must be retained for five years under the AML/CFT Act 2009.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register (online portal at https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A registered company name must consist of letters of the English alphabet, numbers, and specified punctuation only; names in Maori are permitted, but non-Latin script such as Chinese characters is not registrable as the legal name. Any foreign script trading name must be disclosed by way of a filed alternative name registration but does not form part of the legal company name. The legal name of a limited liability company must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd' and must contain no less than three alphabetic characters before the suffix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 20 working days only and is non-renewable. If the Companies Office rejects an application on grounds of similarity, likely confusion, or prohibited token usage, the applicant may submit a fresh application with a new reservation fee, or file a written objection with the Registrar under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993 setting out the basis of distinctiveness and any consent documentation. Where the objection is refused, no internal administrative appeal exists within the Companies Office; the applicant may pursue judicial review proceedings in the High Court of New Zealand within 28 days of notification of refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office must be a physical location within New Zealand that is open and accessible to the public for no fewer than 20 hours per week during ordinary business hours, as required by section 202 of the Companies Act 1993. A pure virtual office or mail-forwarding address without physically accessible premises will be rejected by the Companies Office. For an offshore supply vessel chartering entity, the registered office may be maintained at the premises of a licensed corporate service provider, but the entity must also satisfy the operational substance expectations of Maritime New Zealand for vessel registration and any coastal trading license, which may require a place of business in New Zealand.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High Probability: Unannounced physical inspections by the Department of Internal Affairs (AML/CFT supervisor for non-bank reporting entities) or Maritime New Zealand are assessed at a 60-70% likelihood within the first 12 months of operation, given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier assigned to offshore marine charter activities and the statutory licensing requirement. The inspection may include verification of registered office records, UBO register maintenance, and AML/CFT programme implementation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), in particular sections 10 (incorporation), 14 (notice of incorporation), 16 (constitution), 23 (name restrictions), 91 (written resolutions), 94 (shares with no par value), 151 (director disqualification), 189 (registered office) and 212 (address for service).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, an agency within the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the Companies Register online system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form R-018 - Application for Registration of a Company, lodged electronically through the NZ Companies Register portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement apply under New Zealand law. At least one ordinary share must be issued on incorporation (section 94 of the Companies Act 1993), and shares may be of no par value with consideration being cash, property, services or other lawful consideration. Non-resident ownership of the issued shares is permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF LIMITED, MADE ON ______ 20__. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the authorised share capital of the Company be fixed at one hundred ordinary shares of no par value; that the first subscriber be allotted one fully paid-up ordinary share upon execution of the subscription agreement. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at , New Zealand, and be filed with the Registrar of Companies in compliance with the Companies Act 1993. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED that be and is hereby appointed as sole director of the Company, and be retained as company secretary, each holding office subject to the Companies Act 1993 and any removal by ordinary resolution. 4. BANK AUTHORITY: RESOLVED that the director be authorised to open a corporate bank account in the name of the Company and to sign all mandates and instruction letters. 5. EFFECTIVE DATE: RESOLVED that the foregoing resolutions take effect immediately and be entered in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Due Diligence Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Register online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the New Zealand Companies Register to exclude identical or confusingly similar names under section 23 of the Companies Act 1993. Reserve the proposed name online via the RealMe authenticated portal (fee approximately NZD 20) or proceed directly to incorporation with the confirmed name. Verify that the proposed name does not contain prohibited words or imply a misleading connection with government or regulated industries.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name
Name availability search report
Shareholder identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused under section 23, file a new name application or request a review by the Registrar; the Registrar may also direct a company to change a misleading name under section 26.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Constitution and Subscription Arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and Shareholders under sections 16 and 28 of the Companies Act 1993
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute a written constitution (or formally elect the default First Schedule rules) that provides for share class flexibility, director authority, conflict-of-interest management and permissive non-resident ownership. Execute a share subscription agreement with the initial subscribers and record an allotment decision consistent with the no-minimum-capital regime.
required_dossiers: Constitution or adoption statement for the Companies Act default rules
Share subscription agreement
Consent of each director to act
Shareholding allocation notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any inconsistency between the constitution and the Companies Act 1993; the statutory default rules substitute automatically where the constitution is silent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (online Companies Register via RealMe authenticated portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online application for registration of a company (Form R-018). Enter the company name, registered office address, address for service, director and shareholder details and capital structure. Attach the constitution adoption statement and director consents, pay the statutory filing fee of NZD 118.40 (approximately USD 72) and submit for electronic processing. The system automatically checks each director against disqualification criteria under section 151 of the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: Form R-018 Application for Registration of a Company
Consent to act as director for each director
Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each director
Proof of residential address for each director
Constitution or adoption statement
Certificate of tax compliance if requested by the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a query letter, respond promptly on the Companies Register portal within 10 working days with corrected information; if the application is voided, resubmit the application with a fresh fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon electronic registration, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation under section 14 of the Companies Act 1993 and the company automatically receives a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Download the PDF certificate from the Companies Register, verify the legal entity name and registration date, and preserve the certificate as conclusive evidence of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN registration confirmation
Company extracts from the Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate records inaccurate particulars, file a Form R-018 amendment or request a correction through Companies Office support within the Companies Register portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass unanimous written resolutions in accordance with section 91 of the Companies Act 1993, adopting the pro forma resolution covering share capital subscription, registered office adoption, officer appointments and bank mandate. Maintain minutes and statutory registers at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting or written resolution record
Share certificate issued to the subscriber
Register of directors
Register of shareholders
Declaration of solvency if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer appointment is invalid due to lack of qualification, rectify by a subsequent board resolution and notify the Companies Office within 20 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company in myIR using the NZBN and certificate details to obtain an IRD number. Apply for GST registration if taxable turnover will exceed NZD 60,000 over a 12-month period or voluntarily if the offshore charter business requires input credit recovery. Register for PAYE and KiwiSaver where employees are engaged, and arrange provisional tax payment dates for the upcoming income year.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN letter
Directors IRD numbers
Registered office and physical location details
Business plan or projected turnover calculation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD refuses or delays registration, provide additional charter and ownership documentation via myIR, refer the matter to a licensed tax agent and, if necessary, invoke the statutory dispute resolution procedure under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office, Statutory Records and Maritime Licence Pre-Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and Maritime New Zealand (pre-application stage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is a physical New Zealand street address open to the public during normal business hours, and file the address for service. Initiate the Maritime Transport Operator (MTO) certificate pre-application review with Maritime New Zealand because the business scope (offshore supply vessel leasing and chartering) requires a maritime operating licence. Retain the completed statutory registers at the registered office and make them available for inspection.
required_dossiers: Notice of registered office and address for service
Statutory register file including shareholders and directors
Maritime Transport Operator pre-application form
Vessel particulars or proposed charter-party documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Maritime New Zealand pre-application is queried for insufficient vessel documentation, supplement the filing with ship registration certificates or charter-party excerpts and refile before the submission deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Maritime New Zealand, the Crown entity responsible for maritime safety, security and marine protection, in conjunction with the Environmental Protection Authority and the relevant regional council.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Maritime Transport Operator Certificate (MTO Certificate) issued under Maritime Rules Part 19, together with vessel registration and Certificate of Survey under the Ship Registration Act 1992 and Maritime Rules Part 46.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand under the Exclusive Economic Zone and Continental Shelf (Environmental Effects) Act 2012, coordinated with the relevant Regional Council under the Resource Management Act 1991 for coastal permits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Registration: applicable for offshore marine charter and supply vessel operations (ISIC 5222) that do not involve fixed installations or seabed disturbance; Category 1 - Full EIA Report: triggered only for drilling, seismic support or seabed intervention activities; Category 3 - Exempt: purely administrative leasing absent operational activity. The default tier for this vessel leasing business is Category 2 with a Marine Pollution Prevention Compliance Plan.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with MARPOL Annexes I, IV, V and VI as incorporated by the Marine Protection Rules (Parts 100-130); oil discharge concentration not exceeding 15 ppm for oily water separators; no discharge of sewage within 12 nautical miles of land unless treated; garbage management under Annex V; ballast water management under the Biosecurity (Ballast Water) Regulations 2020; air emissions per the Environmental Standards for Air Pollutants.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for any shore-based office, workshop or storage facility under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; structural engineering inspection and Building Code compliance under the Building Act 2004; workplace safety clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015; Maritime New Zealand Certificate of Survey for each vessel; and crew competency certification under Maritime Rules Part 32.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Te Tari Taake; online portal: MyIR (Secure Online Services)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) from the Companies Office, then apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number and GST registration using the appropriate registration forms (IR596 for non-resident companies or IRD entity registration via MyIR). Non-resident companies may also be required to register under NRWT, FBT, or PAYE if applicable. The GST registration becomes effective from the date of application or the date taxable supplies begin, subject to the NZD 60,000 compulsory registration threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists in New Zealand; entity classification is determined by the Income Tax Act 2007. Available statutory elections include GST grouping elections, provisional tax payment pooling elections, and certain hybrid mismatch ordering elections under subpart FH. There is no free election to reclassify a limited company as pass-through; NZ Limited Companies are taxable entities at the corporate rate.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 annual taxable supplies; voluntary registration available below the threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping. Electronic invoicing in New Zealand is voluntary and operates on the PEPPOL network, facilitated by the NZBN. No API-based fiscal clearance obligation applies; business records may be maintained electronically for GST compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 when the supply is exported or directly connected with exports. For offshore vessel chartering and offshore platform support ship operations, zero-rating applies if the services are supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, or the supply is physically performed outside New Zealand, or the supply directly relates to goods that have been exported or to a vessel used in international transport. Adequate documentary evidence must establish the export/offshore nature of the supply, including contracts, invoices, customs entries, vessel movement records, and evidence of payment from non-resident counterparties.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue audits zero-rated export supplies strictly. If documentary evidence is insufficient or zero-rating has been incorrectly claimed, the full GST amount becomes payable as a shortfall. For fraudulent or fraudulent-intent GST claims, the Tax Administration Act 1994 imposes civil penalties up to 150% of the tax shortfall, late payment penalties and interest, and criminal liability on conviction with fines up to NZD 150,000 for individuals and up to NZD 250,000 for companies, plus potential imprisonment. Retrospective reassessment may claw back incorrectly refunded GST for prior periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full current and capital account convertibility. The New Zealand dollar is freely floating and fully convertible through all registered financial institutions. There are no general exchange controls, no prior approval requirements for profit repatriation, and no prescribed conversion rights or restrictions on capital outflows by non-resident shareholders of a New Zealand limited company. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to tax compliance, principally non-resident withholding tax on dividends or the approved issuer levy, and corporate formalities such as a valid dividend declaration, solvency certification, and submission of the appropriate tax returns. For an offshore supply vessel leasing company, no sector-specific FX conversion or repatriation restriction applies. The Overseas Investment Act 2005 may require consent only if the transaction involves sensitive land or significant business assets; ordinary vessel chartering and leasing do not trigger exchange control screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory surrender rules, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio for export proceeds or foreign currency charter hire receipts. Export proceeds and vessel charter revenues may be retained in any freely convertible currency and settled through any registered New Zealand bank. Banking records must be maintained for anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism purposes under the AML/CFT Act 2009, but no repatriation or conversion obligation exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a primary treasury rail and Medium as an ancillary payment channel. Offshore digital electronic money institutions are not registered New Zealand banks, are not prudentially supervised by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, and cannot be direct participants in the New Zealand high-value or retail clearing systems. They cannot legally hold or settle NZD corporate transactional accounts in the same manner as a licensed New Zealand bank. Legal constraints include the absence of depositor protection, the requirement that all NZD clearing settle through a locally incorporated registered bank, and the need to maintain a qualifying sponsor bank relationship for any inbound or outbound wire activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is legally permissible under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, and directors are not statutorily required to appear physically. In practice, tier-one New Zealand banks will require full KYC due diligence for a non-resident-owned offshore vessel leasing entity, including notarized passport copies, certified copies of constitutional documents, a registered Companies Office extract, evidence of ultimate beneficial ownership, and a board resolution authorizing account opening and signatories. A physical or video compliance interview with the directors or the ultimate beneficial owner is effectively mandatory in most cases, and bank policy may require one in-person visit for enhanced risk profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore supply vessel chartering activity involving counterparties in jurisdictions with higher money laundering or sanctions risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Charter party agreements, vessel registration abstracts, International Safety Management certificates, vessel ownership chain documentation, full corporate KYC profiles of all charterers and counterparties, sanctions screening results, maritime traffic or positioning reports, and independent vessel classification certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated New Zealand company with non-resident directors and no domestic operating history seeking high cross-border transaction limits immediately after incorporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Companies Office certificate of incorporation, register of directors and beneficial owners, constitution, parent company financial statements, bank reference letters from existing financiers, projected cash flow and charter pipeline, board resolutions, source of funds evidence for initial capital, and a detailed business plan for the vessel leasing operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow account being used for third-party charter hire collections and onward payments that could mask trade misinvoicing or layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original invoices, charter hire schedules, bills of lading or equivalent delivery evidence, crewing and agency agreements, vessel tracking records, independent payment reconciliation reports, and contractual documentation linking each transaction to a specific vessel, charterer, and voyage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursements to maritime fuel suppliers, repair yards, insurance brokers, or crew payment processors in high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed disbursement breakdown, supplier due diligence questionnaires, sanctions screening of each beneficiary and vessel, supporting purchase orders and service contracts, statutory declarations explaining commercial rationale, and bank reference confirmation from each receiving institution where available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Profit repatriation or dividend distributions to shareholders residing in jurisdictions with no double tax agreement or perceived tax transparency deficiencies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax residence certificates for all shareholders, signed dividend declarations, Companies Act solvency certificates, current shareholder register, non-resident withholding tax and approved issuer levy payment confirmations, audited financial statements confirming distributable reserves, and a legal opinion confirming economic substance and commercial rationale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed through the New Zealand beneficiary bank using the SWIFT payment network, typically an MT103 customer credit or an MT202 for interbank transfers. The instruction must include the BIC of the receiving New Zealand bank, the company's account number for the capital escrow or operational account, and a purpose code that accurately describes the transaction as an equity injection, shareholder loan, or intercompany loan. The receiving bank will perform full source of funds verification, sanctions screening, AML/CFT customer due diligence, and may require the Companies Office share allotment resolution, an executed loan agreement, and the final beneficial ownership schedule before releasing funds. If the capital injection is linked to vessel acquisition or another transaction requiring consent under the Overseas Investment Act 2005, legal clearance should be obtained before remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outward trade disbursements for vessel operations, bunker fuel, crew wages, insurance premiums, port fees, repair services, and charter-related settlements should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for customer payments or MT202 for bank-to-bank reimbursements. Commercial letters of credit and standby letters of credit opened or confirmed by a tier-one New Zealand bank are the standard clearing rails for major vessel acquisition and leasing disbursements. All outbound instructions must include a compliant purpose code, match supporting invoices and contracts, and pass enhanced due diligence. There is no surrender requirement or exchange control approval for outbound trade payments, but banks will require documentary substantiation to satisfy sanctions, anti-money laundering, and countering financing of terrorism obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forwards with a registered New Zealand bank to hedge NZD/USD charter revenue and lease liabilities
Non-deliverable forwards for third-country currency exposures where the underlying currency is not fully deliverable in the relevant market
Cross-currency interest rate swaps or currency swaps to align USD-denominated vessel debt service cash flows with USD charter receipts
Plain-vanilla foreign exchange option strategies approved by the bank and used solely to hedge commercial exposure arising from offshore supply vessel chartering operations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Companies Office Annual Return (Companies Act 1993, s 214) — current registered office, director, shareholder and constitution particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual — due within 35 working days after the annual return date (the last day of the month of incorporation anniversary); independent of the balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of NZ$100 (approx. USD 60); continued default triggers a Registrar notice of removal and administrative strike-off (Companies Act 1993, s 318); directors liable to prosecution with fines up to NZ$10,000 (approx. USD 6,000)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report to Shareholders (Companies Act 1993, s 208) — board-prepared annual report including the financial statements for the accounting period, auditor's report (if any) and board report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the NZ limited company — not filed with the Companies Office for an SME; the financial statements component is separately filed only where the company is 'large'
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the end of each accounting period, delivered to each shareholder
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors commit an offence for failure to prepare or deliver the annual report and may be fined up to NZ$10,000 (approx. USD 6,000); shareholders may also seek compliance orders

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Auditor's Report (Financial Reporting Act 2013; Companies Act 1993) — mandatory filing for 'large' companies, FMC reporting entities and entities subject to a 5% shareholder audit demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the balance date for the annual reporting cycle — not applicable to non-large SMEs, which prepare but do not file financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be fined up to NZ$10,000 (approx. USD 6,000) for non-delivery; the Registrar may issue a removal notice and strike the company off the Register; non-compliance restricts dividend payments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Offshore Marine Operator Licence and Safety Management System (SMS) audit confirmation — validity of the statutory licence for chartering and operation of offshore platform support vessels (ISIC 5222)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous annual compliance — annual internal SMS audit and confirmation per the licence approval schedule; re-notification required on any change of vessel, operating area or key particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or revocation of the Maritime Transport Operator Licence; prohibition of offshore charter operations; civil and criminal liability for unlicensed operations under the Maritime Transport Act 1994

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit applies if the company is 'large', i.e. it meets any two of: (i) total assets above NZ$60M; (ii) annual revenue above NZ$30M; (iii) 100 or more full-time-equivalent employees. An audit is also required for FMC reporting entities, for certain subsidiaries within overseas group audit/filing requirements, and upon the demand of shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares (cost borne by the company). Otherwise, no compulsory audit applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ IFRS (IFRS-aligned) as issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB); eligible entities may apply the NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR) or the XRB Simplified Accounting Standards for non-publicly-accountable SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Share transfers and director changes must be lodged with the New Zealand Companies Office within 20 working days of the change; the annual return thereafter confirms the ownership and officer positions as at the annual return date. Non-resident share acquisitions may require separate Overseas Investment Office (OIO) screening. New Zealand is transitioning to a statutory beneficial-ownership register; once fully in force, the company will maintain a beneficial-ownership register and confirm it in the annual return, in line with the Companies Office implementation schedule.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Board and Shareholder Meeting Minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 – 500 per annum (NZD 300 – 850) for registered office and registered agent / company secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,800 – 12,000 (NZD 8,000 – 20,000) where a statutory audit is triggered; USD 0 if the company is not 'large' and no shareholder audit demand exists

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions

approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
